summary: Verified tide direction indicator across backend + both frontend surfaces. Backend GET /api/device/folly returns {e, w, dir}; direction is consistent with next-tide letter (currently e[0].y='L' -> dir='out'). Home Weather section shows '▼ Outgoing tide' above the two tide time lines and 'Water 79°F'. Matrix Preview 'Folly Beach tides' frame shows '▼ OUTGOING' (amber) above the tide lines and 'WATER 79°', rendered without cutoff or console errors. All 4 pytest cases pass; UI matches backend on both screens.
critical_code_review_comments: Direction logic is correctly centralized: backend derives dir from events[0].y, and both index.tsx (Weather readout) and matrix-preview.tsx (folly frame) render from folly.dir, so they stay in lockstep.
index.tsx is 3354 lines — over the 700 line guideline; consider splitting the Weather/Sports/TV/Folly/Lake sections into their own components for maintainability (not blocking for this fix).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Live NOAA tide data determines whether the current cycle is 'in' (next=H) or 'out' (next=L). At test time next tide was Low so both surfaces correctly displayed 'Outgoing'. The pytest suite asserts logic consistency (dir matches e[0].y) rather than a specific direction, so it stays valid across tide cycles.
rca_of_issue: N/A — user-reported issue was on the ESP32 panel firmware (not testable in this environment). Verified the backend contract and app-side rendering path used by both the Weather readout and the Matrix Preview folly frame; both are correct.
